brief.contract: n is a positive integer <=5000. Return a plain Python ascending list of distinct positive prime factors, no symbolic objects.
brief.documentation:
Return a sorted list of n's prime factors, ignoring multiplicity
and any composite factor that remains if the limit was set too low
for complete factorization. Unlike factorint(), primefactors() does
not return -1 or 0.

Parameters
==========

n : integer
limit, verbose, **kwargs :
    Additional keyword arguments to be passed to ``factorint``.
    Since ``kwargs`` is new in version 1.13,
    ``limit`` and ``verbose`` are retained for compatibility purposes.

Returns
=======

list(int) : List of prime numbers dividing ``n``

Examples
========

>>> from sympy.ntheory import primefactors, factorint, isprime
>>> primefactors(6)
[2, 3]
>>> primefactors(-5)
[5]

>>> sorted(factorint(123456).items())
[(2, 6), (3, 1), (643, 1)]
>>> primefactors(123456)
[2, 3, 643]

>>> sorted(factorint(10000000001, limit=200).items())
[(101, 1), (99009901, 1)]
>>> isprime(99009901)
False
>>> primefactors(10000000001, limit=300)
[101]

See Also
========

factorint, divisors
